title.en: First-Order Differential Equations, Separable Equations & Existence Theory
title.ar: المعادلات التفاضلية من الرتبة الأولى والمعادلات القابلة للفصل ونظرية الوجود

body.en: A differential equation expresses an intrinsic law of change, connecting an unknown function directly to its own derivatives. In nature and technology, physical laws rarely dictate exact states; instead, they dictate instantaneous rates of progression — cooling rates proportional to temperature differentials, chemical reaction kinetics determined by molecular concentrations, and gravitational acceleration dictating planetary velocities. This foundational chapter develops the analytical theory of first-order differential equations, the method of separation of variables, and the fundamental Picard–Lindelöf Existence and Uniqueness Theorem.
body.ar: A المعادلة التفاضلية expresses an intrinsic law of change, connecting an unknown الدالة directly to its own المشتقات. In nature and technology, physical laws rarely dictate exact states; instead, they dictate instantaneous rates of progression — cooling rates proportional to temperature differentials, chemical reaction kinetics determined by molecular concentrations, and gravitational acceleration dictating planetary velocities. This foundational chapter develops the analytical theory of first-order differential equations, the method of separation of variables, and the fundamental Picard–Lindelöf Existence and Uniqueness Theorem.

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Definition 1.1: Differential Equations, Solutions & Initial Value Problems (IVPs)
label.ar: ● Level 1 Foundation — تعريف 1.1: Differential المعادلات, الحلول & Initial Value Problems (IVPs)

body.en:
An ordinary differential equation (ODE) is an equation relating an unknown single-variable function \( y = y(x) \) to one or more of its derivatives \( y', y'', \dots, y^{(n)} \). The order of the ODE is the order of the highest derivative present.

A solution on an open interval \( I \subseteq \mathbb{R} \) is an \( n \)-times differentiable function \( y(x) \) that identically satisfies the equation for all \( x \in I \). The general solution is the complete family of all possible solutions, containing \( n \) essential arbitrary constants.

An Initial Value Problem (IVP) couples an \( n \)-th order ODE with \( n \) prescribed conditions at a single point \( x_0 \in I \): \[ y(x_0) = y_0, \quad y'(x_0) = y_1, \quad \dots, \quad y^{(n-1)}(x_0) = y_{n-1}. \] A solution satisfying both the differential equation and these initial conditions is designated a particular solution.
body.ar:
An ordinary المعادلة التفاضلية (ODE) is an المعادلة relating an unknown single-المتغير الدالة \( y = y(x) \) to one or more of its المشتقات \( y', y'', \dots, y^{(n)} \). The order of the ODE is the order of the highest المشتقة present.

A solution on an open interval \( I \subseteq \mathbb{R} \) is an \( n \)-times differentiable الدالة \( y(x) \) that identically satisfies the المعادلة for all \( x \in I \). The general solution is the complete family of all possible الحلول, containing \( n \) essential arbitrary constants.

An Initial Value Problem (IVP) couples an \( n \)-th order ODE with \( n \) prescribed conditions at a single point \( x_0 \in I \): \[ y(x_0) = y_0, \quad y'(x_0) = y_1, \quad \dots, \quad y^{(n-1)}(x_0) = y_{n-1}. \] A الحل satisfying both the المعادلة التفاضلية and these initial conditions is designated a particular solution.

label.en: Worked example 1.A — Solution Verification & Interval of Definition
label.ar: مثال محلول 1.A — الحل Verification & Interval of تعريف

body.en:
Verify that \( y(x) = C e^{2x} \) is a solution of \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2y \) for any real constant \( C \), prove that these are the only solutions on \( \mathbb{R} \), and determine the unique solution satisfying \( y(0) = 5 \).

Verification: Differentiating gives \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}[C e^{2x}] = 2C e^{2x} = 2y(x) \), satisfying the ODE for all \( x \in \mathbb{R} \).

Exhaustiveness Proof: Suppose \( y(x) \) is any arbitrary solution to \( y' = 2y \). Consider the product \( u(x) = e^{-2x}y(x) \). Applying the product rule: \[ u'(x) = -2e^{-2x}y(x) + e^{-2x}y'(x) = e^{-2x}\big(y'(x) - 2y(x)\big) = e^{-2x}(0) = 0. \] By the Zero Derivative Theorem (a direct corollary of the Mean Value Theorem), a function whose derivative vanishes on an interval is constant: \( u(x) = C \). Hence \( y(x) = C e^{2x} \), proving no other solutions exist.

Initial Condition: Setting \( x = 0 \): \( y(0) = C e^0 = C = 5 \). The unique particular solution is \( y(x) = 5e^{2x} \).
body.ar:
Verify that \( y(x) = C e^{2x} \) is a الحل of \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2y \) for any real الثابت \( C \), prove that these are the only الحلول on \( \mathbb{R} \), and حدّد unique الحل satisfying \( y(0) = 5 \).

Verification: Differentiating gives \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}[C e^{2x}] = 2C e^{2x} = 2y(x) \), satisfying the ODE for all \( x \in \mathbb{R} \).

Exhaustiveness برهان: Suppose \( y(x) \) is any arbitrary الحل to \( y' = 2y \). Consider the product \( u(x) = e^{-2x}y(x) \). Applying the product rule: \[ u'(x) = -2e^{-2x}y(x) + e^{-2x}y'(x) = e^{-2x}\big(y'(x) - 2y(x)\big) = e^{-2x}(0) = 0. \] By the Zero المشتقة مبرهنة (a direct corollary of the Mean Value مبرهنة), a الدالة whose المشتقة vanishes on an interval is الثابت: \( u(x) = C \). ومنه \( y(x) = C e^{2x} \), proving no other الحلول exist.

Initial Condition: Setting \( x = 0 \): \( y(0) = C e^0 = C = 5 \). The unique particular الحل is \( y(x) = 5e^{2x} \).

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Definition 1.2: Autonomous & Separable Differential Equations
label.ar: ● Level 1 Foundation — تعريف 1.2: Autonomous & Separable Differential المعادلات

body.en:
A first-order differential equation is separable if the derivative factors into an explicit function of \( x \) multiplied by an explicit function of \( y \): \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = f(x)\,g(y). \]

An ODE is autonomous if the independent variable does not appear explicitly: \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = g(y) \). Any real value \( y^* \) such that \( g(y^*) = 0 \) produces a constant solution \( y(x) \equiv y^* \), termed an equilibrium solution (or critical point). Geometrically, equilibrium solutions correspond to horizontal integral curves in the \( xy \)-plane.
body.ar:
A first-order المعادلة التفاضلية is separable if the المشتقة factors into an explicit الدالة of \( x \) multiplied by an explicit الدالة of \( y \): \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = f(x)\,g(y). \]

An ODE is autonomous if the independent المتغير does not appear explicitly: \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = g(y) \). Any real value \( y^* \) such that \( g(y^*) = 0 \) produces a الثابت الحل \( y(x) \equiv y^* \), termed an equilibrium solution (or critical point). Geometrically, التوازن الحلول correspond to horizontal التكامل curves in the \( xy \)-plane.

value.en: Locate all roots of \( g(y) = 0 \). Every real root \( y = y^* \) is a constant equilibrium solution that must be recorded before division to avoid singular division by zero.

label.ar: 2. Differential Separation (المعادلات التفاضلية من الرتبة الأولى والمعادلات القابلة للفصل ونظرية الوجود)

value.en: On intervals where \( g(y) \neq 0 \), rewrite the equation in differential form: \( \frac{1}{g(y)}\,dy = f(x)\,dx \).

label.ar: 3. Indefinite Integration (المعادلات التفاضلية من الرتبة الأولى والمعادلات القابلة للفصل ونظرية الوجود)

value.en: Integrate both differentials: \( \int \frac{1}{g(y)}\,dy = \int f(x)\,dx + C \). A single arbitrary constant \( C \) suffices, as constants of integration combine.
Invert the algebraic relation to solve explicitly for \( y(x) \) where possible, and determine the maximal open interval of existence \( I \) containing the initial point.

label.en: ▲ Level 2 Analytical Theorem 1.1 — Separation on Nonzero Branches
label.ar: ▲ Level 2 Analytical مبرهنة 1.1 — Separation on Nonzero Branches

body.en: Let \( I, J \subseteq \mathbb{R} \) be open intervals. Suppose \( f: I \to \mathbb{R} \) is continuous and \( g: J \to \mathbb{R} \) is continuous with \( g(y) \neq 0 \) for all \( y \in J \). Let \( F(x) \) be an antiderivative of \( f(x) \) on \( I \), and let \( G(y) \) be an antiderivative of \( 1/g(y) \) on \( J \). A differentiable function \( y: I \to J \) satisfies \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = f(x)\,g(y) \] if and only if there exists a constant \( C \in \mathbb{R} \) such that \[ G(y(x)) = F(x) + C. \]
body.ar: Let \( I, J \subseteq \mathbb{R} \) be open intervals. Suppose \( f: I \to \mathbb{R} \) is continuous and \( g: J \to \mathbb{R} \) is continuous with \( g(y) \neq 0 \) for all \( y \in J \). Let \( F(x) \) be an antiderivative of \( f(x) \) on \( I \), and let \( G(y) \) be an antiderivative of \( 1/g(y) \) on \( J \). A differentiable الدالة \( y: I \to J \) satisfies \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = f(x)\,g(y) \] if and only if there exists a الثابت \( C \in \mathbb{R} \) such that \[ G(y(x)) = F(x) + C. \]

body.en:
Sufficiency (⇒): Suppose \( y(x) \) satisfies the ODE with \( y(x) \in J \). Since \( g(y(x)) \neq 0 \), divide by \( g(y(x)) \): \[ \frac{1}{g(y(x))}\,y'(x) = f(x). \] By the Chain Rule, \( \dfrac{d}{dx}[G(y(x))] = G'(y(x))\,y'(x) = \dfrac{1}{g(y(x))}\,y'(x) \). Thus: \[ \frac{d}{dx}[G(y(x))] = \frac{d}{dx}[F(x)]. \] Integrating both sides with respect to \( x \) yields \( G(y(x)) - F(x) = C \), so \( G(y(x)) = F(x) + C \).

Necessity (⇐): Conversely, suppose \( G(y(x)) = F(x) + C \). Differentiating both sides with respect to \( x \) using the Chain Rule yields: \[ G'(y(x))\,y'(x) = F'(x) \implies \frac{1}{g(y(x))}\,y'(x) = f(x). \] Multiplying by \( g(y(x)) \) yields \( y'(x) = f(x)\,g(y(x)) \), completing the proof.
body.ar:
Sufficiency (⇒): Suppose \( y(x) \) satisfies the ODE with \( y(x) \in J \). Since \( g(y(x)) \neq 0 \), divide by \( g(y(x)) \): \[ \frac{1}{g(y(x))}\,y'(x) = f(x). \] By the Chain Rule, \( \dfrac{d}{dx}[G(y(x))] = G'(y(x))\,y'(x) = \dfrac{1}{g(y(x))}\,y'(x) \). وعليه: \[ \frac{d}{dx}[G(y(x))] = \frac{d}{dx}[F(x)]. \] Integrating both sides بالنسبة إلى \( x \) yields \( G(y(x)) - F(x) = C \), so \( G(y(x)) = F(x) + C \).

Necessity (⇐): Conversely, suppose \( G(y(x)) = F(x) + C \). Differentiating both sides بالنسبة إلى \( x \) using the Chain Rule yields: \[ G'(y(x))\,y'(x) = F'(x) \implies \frac{1}{g(y(x))}\,y'(x) = f(x). \] Multiplying by \( g(y(x)) \) yields \( y'(x) = f(x)\,g(y(x)) \), completing the proof.

label.en: Worked example 1.B — Initial Value Problems & Finite-Time Blowup
label.ar: مثال محلول 1.B — Initial Value Problems & Finite-Time Blowup

body.en:
Solve the initial value problem \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x y^2, \qquad y(0) = 1, \] and determine its maximal open interval of valid existence.

Step 1: Check equilibrium: \( g(y) = y^2 = 0 \implies y \equiv 0 \). Since \( y(0) = 1 \neq 0 \), the solution lies on the positive branch \( y > 0 \).

Step 2: Separate and integrate: \[ \int y^{-2}\,dy = \int 2x\,dx \implies -\frac{1}{y} = x^2 + C. \] Applying \( y(0) = 1 \): \( -\frac{1}{1} = 0^2 + C \implies C = -1 \).

Step 3: Solve for \( y(x) \): \[ -\frac{1}{y} = x^2 - 1 \implies y(x) = \frac{1}{1 - x^2}. \]

Step 4: Maximal interval of existence: The function \( y(x) = \frac{1}{1 - x^2} \) has vertical asymptotes at \( x = \pm 1 \). Because a solution to an ODE must be continuous on an interval containing the initial point \( x_0 = 0 \), the maximal interval of existence is strictly: \[ I = (-1, 1). \] As \( x \to 1^- \) or \( x \to -1^+ \), \( y(x) \to +\infty \). This phenomenon is known as finite-time blowup, demonstrating that even when the ODE's right-hand side \( f(x, y) = 2x y^2 \) is infinitely smooth everywhere on \( \mathbb{R}^2 \), solutions to non-linear equations can cease to exist in finite time.
body.ar:
Solve the initial value problem \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x y^2, \qquad y(0) = 1, \] and determine its maximal open interval of valid existence.

Step 1: Check التوازن: \( g(y) = y^2 = 0 \implies y \equiv 0 \). Since \( y(0) = 1 \neq 0 \), the الحل lies on the positive branch \( y > 0 \).

Step 2: Separate and integrate: \[ \int y^{-2}\,dy = \int 2x\,dx \implies -\frac{1}{y} = x^2 + C. \] Applying \( y(0) = 1 \): \( -\frac{1}{1} = 0^2 + C \implies C = -1 \).

Step 3: أوجد قيمة \( y(x) \): \[ -\frac{1}{y} = x^2 - 1 \implies y(x) = \frac{1}{1 - x^2}. \]

Step 4: Maximal interval of existence: The الدالة \( y(x) = \frac{1}{1 - x^2} \) has vertical خطوط التقارب at \( x = \pm 1 \). Because a الحل to an ODE must be continuous on an interval containing the initial point \( x_0 = 0 \), the maximal interval of existence is strictly: \[ I = (-1, 1). \] As \( x \to 1^- \) or \( x \to -1^+ \), \( y(x) \to +\infty \). This phenomenon is known as finite-time blowup, demonstrating that even عندما the ODE's right-hand side \( f(x, y) = 2x y^2 \) is infinitely smooth everywhere on \( \mathbb{R}^2 \), الحلول to non-المعادلات الخطية can cease to exist in finite time.

label.en: Worked example 1.C — Analytical Application: Logistic Growth & Critical Harvesting Threshold
label.ar: مثال محلول 1.C — Analytical Application: Logistic Growth & Critical Harvesting Threshold

body.en:
A biological population \( P(t) \) with carrying capacity \( K \) and intrinsic growth rate \( r \) is subject to a constant harvesting rate \( H > 0 \): \[ \frac{dP}{dt} = r P\left(1 - \frac{P}{K}\right) - H. \] Determine the critical harvesting threshold \( H_{\text{crit}} \) above which population collapse is inevitable.

Equilibrium Analysis: Set \( \frac{dP}{dt} = 0 \): \[ -\frac{r}{K}P^2 + r P - H = 0 \implies r P^2 - r K P + K H = 0. \] The roots are given by the quadratic formula: \[ P_{1, 2} = \frac{r K \pm \sqrt{r^2 K^2 - 4 r K H}}{2r} = \frac{K}{2} \left(1 \pm \sqrt{1 - \frac{4H}{rK}}\right). \]

Saddle-Node Bifurcation: The discriminant \( \Delta = r^2 K^2 - 4rKH \) dictates the physical dynamics:

  • If \( H < \frac{rK}{4} \): Two real equilibria exist: a stable carrying capacity \( P_1 \) and an unstable threshold \( P_2 \). If \( P(0) > P_2 \), the population stabilizes at \( P_1 \).
  • If \( H = H_{\text{crit}} = \frac{rK}{4} \): A single semi-stable equilibrium exists at \( P = K/2 \).
  • If \( H > \frac{rK}{4} \): \( \Delta < 0 \), so \( \frac{dP}{dt} < 0 \) for all \( P \ge 0 \). No equilibria exist, and the population drops to 0 in finite time.

Hence, the maximum sustainable yield is precisely \( H_{\text{crit}} = \frac{rK}{4} \).

label.en: ▲ Level 3 University Rigor — Theorem 1.2: Picard–Lindelöf Existence and Uniqueness Theorem
label.ar: ▲ Level 3 University Rigor — مبرهنة 1.2: Picard–Lindelöf Existence and Uniqueness مبرهنة

body.en:
Consider the initial value problem \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y), \qquad y(x_0) = y_0. \] Let \( R = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x - x_0| \le a, \, |y - y_0| \le b\} \) be a closed rectangle centered at \( (x_0, y_0) \). Suppose:

  1. \( f(x, y) \) is continuous on \( R \), so it is bounded by \( M = \max_{(x,y)\in R} |f(x, y)| < \infty \).
  2. \( f(x, y) \) satisfies a Lipschitz condition in \( y \) on \( R \): there exists \( L > 0 \) such that \[ |f(x, y_1) - f(x, y_2)| \le L |y_1 - y_2| \quad \forall (x, y_1), (x, y_2) \in R. \] (A continuous partial derivative \( \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} \) on \( R \) guarantees this with \( L = \max_R |\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}| \)).

Then the IVP has a unique continuously differentiable solution \( y(x) \) defined on the interval \( [x_0 - h, x_0 + h] \), where \( h = \min\{a, \frac{b}{M}\} \).

Picard Successive Iteration Operator: Converting the IVP into an equivalent Volterra integral equation \[ y(x) = y_0 + \int_{x_0}^x f(t, y(t))\,dt, \] the sequence defined by \( y_0(x) = y_0 \) and \[ y_{k+1}(x) = y_0 + \int_{x_0}^x f(t, y_k(t))\,dt \] converges uniformly on \( [x_0 - h, x_0 + h] \) to the unique solution by the Banach Fixed-Point Contraction Principle.

Pathological Breakdown of Uniqueness: Consider \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 3 y^{2/3} \) with \( y(0) = 0 \). Here \( f(x, y) = 3y^{2/3} \) is continuous on \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) (so Peano's Theorem guarantees existence). However, \[ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = 2y^{-1/3} \] is unbounded as \( y \to 0 \), violating the Lipschitz condition. Separating variables gives \( y(x) = x^3 \), but \( y(x) \equiv 0 \) is also a solution! In fact, for any \( c > 0 \), the family \[ y(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & x \le c \\ (x - c)^3 & x > c \end{cases} \] is continuously differentiable and satisfies the IVP, yielding infinitely many solutions originating from \( (0, 0) \).
body.ar:
Consider the initial value problem \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y), \qquad y(x_0) = y_0. \] Let \( R = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x - x_0| \le a, \, |y - y_0| \le b\} \) be a closed rectangle centered at \( (x_0, y_0) \). Suppose:

Here \( f(x, y) = 3y^{2/3} \) is continuous on \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) (so Peano's مبرهنة guarantees existence). However, \[ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = 2y^{-1/3} \] is unbounded as \( y \to 0 \), violating the Lipschitz condition. Separating المتغيرات gives \( y(x) = x^3 \), but \( y(x) \equiv 0 \) is also a الحل! In fact, for any \( c > 0 \), the family \[ y(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & x \le c \\ (x - c)^3 & x > c \end{cases} \] is continuously differentiable and satisfies the IVP, yielding infinitely many solutions originating from \( (0, 0) \).

label.ar: ⚠️ أخطاء شائعة ومصائد جامعية — Lost Singular الحلول & Non-Linear Intervals

body.en:
Dividing by zero drops equilibrium solutions: When separating \( \frac{dy}{dx} = g(y)h(x) \) by dividing by \( g(y) \), you assume \( g(y) \neq 0 \). Any constant value \( y = k \) where \( g(k) = 0 \) is a valid equilibrium solution that will not appear in the separated integral unless checked separately!

Constant of integration placement: You must add the constant \( +C \) immediately after performing integration. For example, in \( \ln|y| = 2x + C \), exponentiating gives \( |y| = e^{2x+C} = e^C e^{2x} = A e^{2x} \), NOT \( e^{2x} + C \).

Finite-Time Blowup & Maximal Interval: In linear equations, solutions are guaranteed to exist wherever the coefficient functions are continuous. In non-linear equations, solutions frequently experience finite-time singularities (blowup) within bounded domains, requiring explicit verification of the maximal open interval of existence.

question.en: Solve the initial value problem \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x(y^2 + 1) \) with \( y(0) = 1 \), and determine its maximal interval of existence.
question.ar: حل the initial value problem \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x(y^2 + 1) \) with \( y(0) = 1 \), and حدّد its maximal interval of existence.

solution.en:
Step 1: Separate variables: \[ \frac{1}{y^2 + 1}\,dy = 2x\,dx. \]

Step 2: Integrate both sides: \[ \int \frac{1}{y^2 + 1}\,dy = \int 2x\,dx \implies \arctan(y) = x^2 + C. \]

Step 3: Apply the initial condition \( y(0) = 1 \): \[ \arctan(1) = 0^2 + C \implies C = \frac{\pi}{4}. \]

Step 4: Solve explicitly for \( y(x) \): \[ y(x) = \tan\left(x^2 + \frac{\pi}{4}\right). \]

Step 5: Interval of existence: The tangent function has vertical asymptotes where its argument equals \( \pm \frac{\pi}{2} \). To contain \( x_0 = 0 \): \[ -\frac{\pi}{2} < x^2 + \frac{\pi}{4} < \frac{\pi}{2} \implies -\frac{3\pi}{4} < x^2 < \frac{\pi}{4}. \] Since \( x^2 \ge 0 \), the constraint is \( x^2 < \frac{\pi}{4} \implies x \in \left(-\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\right) \).

question.en: Find all equilibrium solutions to \( \frac{dy}{dx} = y(4 - y) - 3 \), classify their stability, and find the particular solution passing through \( y(0) = 2 \).
question.ar: أوجد all equilibrium solutions to \( \frac{dy}{dx} = y(4 - y) - 3 \), classإذا كانy their stability, and أوجد الحل الخاص passing through \( y(0) = 2 \).

solution.en:
Step 1: Locate equilibria: \[ -y^2 + 4y - 3 = 0 \implies (y - 1)(3 - y) = 0 \implies y_1 = 1, \quad y_2 = 3. \]

Step 2: Stability via derivative: Let \( f(y) = -y^2 + 4y - 3 \). Then \( f'(y) = -2y + 4 \).
At \( y = 1 \), \( f'(1) = 2 > 0 \implies y = 1 \) is an unstable source.
At \( y = 3 \), \( f'(3) = -2 < 0 \implies y = 3 \) is a stable sink.

Step 3: Separate variables for IVP \( y(0) = 2 \): \[ \frac{1}{(y - 1)(3 - y)}\,dy = dx \implies \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{y - 1} + \frac{1}{3 - y}\right)dy = dx. \] Integrating: \[ \frac{1}{2}\big(\ln|y - 1| - \ln|3 - y|\big) = x + C_1 \implies \ln\left|\frac{y - 1}{3 - y}\right| = 2x + C_2. \]

Applying \( y(0) = 2 \): \( \ln|1/1| = 0 = 0 + C_2 \implies C_2 = 0 \). Since \( 1 < y < 3 \), \( \frac{y - 1}{3 - y} = e^{2x} \). Solving for \( y \): \[ y(x) = \frac{1 + 3e^{2x}}{1 + e^{2x}}. \] Note that as \( x \to \infty \), \( y(x) \to 3 \), verifying convergence to the stable equilibrium sink.

question.en: Compute the first three Picard successive approximations \( y_1(x), y_2(x), y_3(x) \) for the initial value problem \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x(1 + y) \) with \( y(0) = 0 \), and identify the Taylor series of the exact solution.
question.ar: Compute the first three Picard successive approximations \( y_1(x), y_2(x), y_3(x) \) for the initial value problem \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x(1 + y) \) with \( y(0) = 0 \), and identإذا كانy the Taylor series of the exact solution.

solution.en:
Picard Integral Operator: \[ y_{k+1}(x) = y_0 + \int_0^x 2t\big(1 + y_k(t)\big)\,dt, \qquad y_0(x) = 0. \]

Iterate 1: \[ y_1(x) = 0 + \int_0^x 2t(1 + 0)\,dt = \left[t^2\right]_0^x = x^2. \]

Iterate 2: \[ y_2(x) = \int_0^x 2t(1 + t^2)\,dt = \int_0^x (2t + 2t^3)\,dt = x^2 + \frac{x^4}{2}. \]

Iterate 3: \[ y_3(x) = \int_0^x 2t\left(1 + t^2 + \frac{t^4}{2}\right)dt = \int_0^x (2t + 2t^3 + t^5)\,dt = x^2 + \frac{x^4}{2} + \frac{x^6}{6}. \]

Exact Solution: By inspection, \[ y_k(x) = \sum_{m=1}^k \frac{(x^2)^m}{m!} \xrightarrow{k\to\infty} e^{x^2} - 1. \] Verifying by separation: \( \frac{dy}{1+y} = 2x\,dx \implies \ln|1+y| = x^2 \implies y(x) = e^{x^2} - 1 \), confirming uniform convergence of the Picard approximations.

question.en: [Practice 4 · Easy] Consider the separable differential equation \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x \) with the initial condition \( y(0) = 3 \). Find the value of \( y(2) \).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Easy] Consider the separable dإذا كانferential equation \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x \) with the initial condition \( y(0) = 3 \). أوجد قيمة \( y(2) \).

hints.en: This is a separable equation. We can rewrite it as \( dy = 2x \, dx \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( dy = 2x \, dx \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Substituting \(x = 2\) into the particular solution, we have \(y(2) = (2)^2 + 3 = 4 + 3\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(x = 2\) ، \(y(2) = (2)^2 + 3 = 4 + 3\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en: The differential equation is \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x \). This is a separable equation. We can rewrite it as \( dy = 2x \, dx \). Integrating both sides gives \( \int dy = \int 2x \, dx \), which results in \( y = x^2 + C \), where C is the constant of integration. We are given the initial condition \( y(0) = 3 \). Substituting these values into the general solution, we get \( 3 = (0)^2 + C \), so \( C = 3 \). Therefore, the particular solution is \( y = x^2 + 3 \). We need to find the value of \( y(2) \). Substituting \( x = 2 \) into the particular solution, we have \( y(2) = (2)^2 + 3 = 4 + 3 = 7 \).
